task_row_model.query: For a planned two-arm randomized trial of a 12-week cognitive behavioral intervention, specify an appropriate primary outcome, a sample size calculation with assumptions and total enrollment target, and the primary statistical analysis approach.

documents.content: In trials of psychological interventions for depressive symptoms, the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) is commonly designated as the primary outcome. We defined the primary endpoint as the continuous change in PHQ-9 score from baseline to week 12, measured by trained assessors blind to allocation. Baseline assessment occurs immediately prior to randomization; the week-12 assessment is the primary timepoint for efficacy comparison. Continuous change preserves statistical power compared with dichotomous responder definitions and aligns with established psychometric practice in primary care and community mental health randomized controlled trials.
documents.reasoning_trace: Provides primary outcome definition (PHQ-9 change) and timing (baseline to 12 weeks).

documents.content: Sample size was calculated for a two-arm parallel randomized trial comparing intervention versus usual care on the week-12 PHQ-9 change score. We powered the study to detect a mean difference of 3.0 points with an assumed common standard deviation of 6.0, using a two-sided alpha of 0.05 and 90% power. This yields approximately 85 participants per group before attrition. Allowing for 20% loss to follow-up inflates the required enrollment to 106 per group, so the trial should enroll 212 participants in total to preserve power for the primary comparison at 12 weeks.
documents.reasoning_trace: Contains the sample size assumptions, calculation result (85 per group) and final enrollment target (212).

documents.content: The primary analysis will follow intention-to-treat principles including all randomized participants in their assigned groups. We will use a linear mixed-effects model for repeated measures to compare groups, adjusting for baseline PHQ-9 score and including fixed effects for treatment, time and a treatment-by-time interaction; participant-level random intercepts will account for within-subject correlation. The primary inference is the estimated adjusted difference in mean PHQ-9 change at week 12. Missing outcome data will be addressed using multiple imputation under a missing-at-random assumption, with secondary sensitivity analyses using pattern‑mixture models to assess robustness to departures from MAR.
documents.reasoning_trace: Specifies ITT, LMM with baseline adjustment and treatment×time interaction, and missing-data procedures (MI, pattern-mixture).

documents.content: Cognitive behavioral approaches have a long history dating to the 1960s; press summaries frequently highlight broad population-level prevalence figures and evocative patient stories. Attention-grabbing statistics (e.g., lifetime prevalence estimates) and clinician quotes often appear alongside case vignettes of individual recovery trajectories. Such materials typically emphasize real-world uptake, training pathways, and policy context rather than protocol specifics. While useful for stakeholder engagement and dissemination, these accounts rarely provide the statistical assumptions or formal analysis plans needed for trial design and inference.
documents.reasoning_trace: Contextual noise: historical background, prevalence statistics, and anecdotes not used for planning specifics.

task_row_model.golden_answer: Primary outcome: change in PHQ-9 score from baseline to 12 weeks. Sample size: two-arm parallel RCT powered to detect a 3.0-point mean difference (SD=6.0) with two-sided alpha=0.05 and 90% power (85 per group); inflating 20% attrition yields 106 per group, 212 total. Primary analysis: intention-to-treat linear mixed-effects model adjusted for baseline PHQ-9 with a treatment×time interaction estimating the 12-week difference; missing data handled by multiple imputation (MAR) with pattern‑mixture sensitivity analyses.
